Fish landing sites: geometry vs the degrees-minutes text field (m)median 0.0, max 0.0 (11 parsed)
Turtle nesting sites: geometry vs Lat/Lon attributes (m)median 0.0, max 0.0 (34 sites)
Outcrop lines inside the study area: distance to nearest ACA reef pixel (400 sample points)median 614 m, 31% within 100 m
Heat stress daily series: dates and gaps2017-01-01 to 2026-10-09, 3568 days, 1 gaps
DHW recomputed from sea-surface temperature and the 28.78 C threshold vs the filemax difference 0.004 C-weeks; SST range 24.7 to 30.8 C
Heat-stress limitsRegional average of 0.25 degree satellite SST within 50 km of the port, baseline 1985 to 2012; DHW for the first 84 days of 2017 lacks its lead-in (no stress was recorded then). Not the NOAA Coral Reef Watch product.
Correction to my earlier workMy earlier Earth Engine script labelled two Allen Coral Atlas benthic classes the wrong way round (15 as microalgal mats, 18 as coral/algae). The atlas class table has 15 = Coral/Algae and 18 = Microalgal mats. This dashboard uses the correct labels; the old reef_habitat_area.csv names for those two classes are swapped.
Outcrop linesThe county layer named Coral_Reefs has 156 of 204 lines labelled "rock", the rest blank, and only 31% of sample points on its lines inside the study area lie within 100 m of the atlas reef extent, so it is drawn as outcrop lines and not counted as coral.
Missing dataThe marine turbidity export was not in the data pack, so no water-quality series is shown.
Area figuresHabitat areas are counted on the 5 m source raster inside each zone; the map overlay is resampled to 10 m and its class areas differ by up to 5% from the source.
Not testable offlineAlignment against live basemap tiles. Overlays use the same Web Mercator grid as the tiles; registration against the source rasters is tested above. Check the port marker against the basemap when you open the file.
Validation: heat-stress sensitivityMoving the warm-month threshold (28.78 C) by 0.15 C either way keeps the ranking, 2024 above 2020 above every other year, and keeps 2020 and 2024 as the only years reaching an alert level (2024 peak 10.0 to 12.6; 2020 peak 4.2 to 7.1). Lowering it by 0.3 C would also lift 2025 to alert level 1 (peak 4.9).
Validation: baseline and warmingThe warmest monthly mean exceeded the 1985–2012 threshold in 8 of 9 full years (2017–2025; only 2021, at 28.73, did not), so degree heating weeks partly reflect warming since the baseline and not only year-to-year anomalies. April is the warmest month (2017–2026 mean 29.34 C).
Validation: algorithmDegree heating weeks recomputed independently from the daily temperatures (84-day sum of daily excess over the threshold when at least 1 C, divided by 7) match the file to 0.004 C-weeks.
Validation: distances and coordinatesStraight-line distances in UTM differ from geodesic by at most 0.04% on every point layer; fish landing and turtle coordinates match their own latitude and longitude fields to 0.1 m.

Habitat: Allen Coral Atlas v2.0, 5 m, from 2018–2020 PlanetScope composites (CC BY 4.0); shown here at 10 m. "Coral/algae" means hard-bottom habitat supporting living coral and/or algae, not a measure of live coral cover, and there is no way to tell change over time from this single map. Heat stress: degree heating weeks (DHW) estimated from satellite sea-surface temperature averaged within 50 km of the port against the warmest-month average of 1985–2012; this is an estimate, not NOAA Coral Reef Watch's own product. DHW of 4 or more is bleaching-alert level 1 and 8 or more is level 2. Moving the threshold by 0.15 C either way keeps the finding that only 2020 and 2024 reach an alert level; the warmest monthly mean exceeded the 1985 to 2012 threshold in eight of nine full years, so part of the signal is long-term warming. Fish landing sites were surveyed in 2009; turtle records are from June to December 2019; dolphin school records are undated. The layer named Coral_Reefs in the county database is labelled "rock" in its attributes and agrees with the atlas reef extent only partly, so it is shown as outcrop lines. A marine turbidity series was planned but was not in the data pack, so it is not shown. Basemaps © OpenStreetMap contributors, CARTO, Esri, OpenTopoMap, Mapbox.
